summary: Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at Ryukoku University and as president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University under Gyōō Kageyama around 1934–1937. He later held posts at Rissho University (~1949–1984) and Minobusan University (~1972–1980).
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.

Eiun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2006). He served as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2015) and an assistant professor at Musashino University (~2015).

Ekai Kawaguchi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Gyosei Shoin, Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College under teachers including Hiroshi Tsuchiya and Sarat Chandra Das. He taught at Toyo University (1916), Taisho University (~1926–1934), and Toyo Bunko (1940).

Eki Nakayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2020) and held a DC2 special research fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2020).
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji-ha Shogakuin (attested 1998).

Eleanor Rosch is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Reed College (~1956–1960) and Harvard University (~1964–1969). She joined the University of California, Berkeley around 1971.
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a scholar in Tibetology. She has held posts at the University of Bonn and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1997).
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Charles Hallisey.

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen and later held posts there (2016–2017, attested 2022). In 2020, she was Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen.

Eli Franco works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto University, La Trobe University, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna, becoming director of the Institut für Indologie und Zentralasienwissenschaften at Leipzig University around 2005.

Elijah Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (PhD ~2000–2007) under Geshe Karma Sonam, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Charles Hallisey.

Eliot Deutsch was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Columbia University (~1956–1960). He was a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1967–2015), editor of Philosophy East and West (~1967–1988), and held posts at Harvard, Chicago, and Cambridge.

Elisa Freschi works in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Raffaele Torella (~2003–2007). She has held posts at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna, and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Würzburg (~1958–1963) and University of Münster (~1967–1970). She held posts at the University of Notre Dame (~1970–1985) and Harvard University (~1988).

Elizabeth Ann Cecil, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, earned degrees from Hastings College, University of Tennessee, and Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald. She held posts at Groningen, Baroda College, Leiden University, and Florida State University (~2019).
Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Oxford by 1999, studying under Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at SOAS University of London under Adrian David Hugh Bivar (~1980–1987). She served as a curator at the British Museum (~1992–2017).

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Canterbury by 1994. She served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).
